title: Feature-aligned spend lifecycle sheet
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a feature-aligned QBR working worksheet to map token spend and rate-limit symptoms back to product features and engineering routes. Use it to prepare a 10–15 minute QBR slide: what caused spend variance, which routes are risky for rate limits, and short/medium-term remediation recommendations.

How to use:
- Populate the table rows with each externally-billable feature or API surface (e.g., chat-stream, batch-embeddings, summarization-batch, auto-tagging).
- For each feature, include both usage metrics and qualitative notes about recent config changes, model variants, or rollout events.
- Use the summary rows at the bottom to calculate projected monthly spend and identify features exceeding threshold.

Column headers (spreadsheet view):
1) Feature Name
2) Endpoint / Route (example path)
3) Primary Model (e.g., gpt-redi-13b-q4)
4) Avg tokens per call (p50)
5) Calls/day (30d avg)
6) Tokens/day (formula: 4 * 5)
7) Cost per 1k tokens (USD)
8) Estimated cost/day (formula: 6/1000 * 7)
9) 30d spend (formula: 8 * 30)
10) Rate-limit incidents (30d count)
11) Major recent changes (release, prompt rework, caching disabled)
12) Suggested QBR talking point (one-liner)
13) Recommended action (short term)
14) Owner / Eng contact

Sample rows (copy into sheet):
- Feature Name: In-product Chat Assist
  Endpoint: /v1/chat/generate
  Primary Model: redwood-chat-7b-q4
  Avg tokens per call: 420
  Calls/day: 12,400
  Tokens/day: 5,208,000
  Cost per 1k tokens: $0.0025
  Estimated cost/day: $13.02
  30d spend: $390.6
  Rate-limit incidents: 6
  Major recent changes: Canary rolled new prompt template on 2025-02-18; prefix caching paused for debug 2025-02-20
  Suggested QBR talking point: Spend spike tied to canary and cache pause; recommend revert or increase caching TTL
  Recommended action: Re-enable prefix cache and schedule A/B with reduced prompt length; monitor 48h
  Owner: eng-products/chat-team@redwood.com

- Feature Name: Bulk Embedding Job (analytics)
  Endpoint: /v1/embeddings/batch
  Primary Model: embed-xl-2
  Avg tokens per call: 12,800
  Calls/day: 78
  Tokens/day: 998,400
  Cost per 1k tokens: $0.0009
  Estimated cost/day: $0.90
  30d spend: $27.0
  Rate-limit incidents: 0
  Major recent changes: Large one-off migration on 2025-02-10 (no dedupe)
  Suggested QBR talking point: One-off migration explains jump; add dedupe and backfill throttles
  Recommended action: Implement dedupe and add burst-capacity gating; schedule next refresh window
  Owner: data-platform@redwood.com

Custom thresholds and alerts (suggested):
- Feature-level monthly spend redline: $1,500 (notify CS + AE)
- Daily % increase trigger: >40% day-over-day or >200% week-over-week (auto-create ticket)
- Rate-limit incident threshold: >5 incidents in 30d -> escalate to SRE + product
- Token-per-call regression: >25% increase vs baseline -> add to regression alert suite

QBR summary rows to prepare for customer slides:
- Total 30d billable spend (sum of 30d spend column)
- Top 3 cost drivers (features with highest 30d spend)
- Top 3 risk drivers (features with highest rate-limit incident counts or largest token-per-call regressions)
- Actions taken since last QBR (list from Recommended action column where done = yes)
- Open asks for customer (e.g., confirm retention policy, approve limited bot change window)

Analysis notes / formula hints for CS use:
- If you see repeated small-rate-limit incidents on a single route, check client-side exponential backoff and batching; often a 5–10% reduction in calls/day or a 20% increase in backoff window reduces incidents by >50%.
- For embeddings-heavy customers, check whether feature-level deduplication (client-side hash) could save 10–40% of tokens.
- Use cost-per-1k tokens to simulate impact of model-switch: new_cost/day = tokens/day/1000 * new_cost_per_1k

Playbook snippets (short-term -> medium-term):
- Short-term (within 48h): re-enable caching, add temporary rate cap, add budget alert to customer portal, notify AE and CS manager
- Medium-term (2–6 weeks): rework prompts to reduce prefix length, shift to smaller model for low-quality contexts, implement batching or debounce in SDKs
- Long-term (quarter): move heavy workloads to dedicated capacity reservation, add compute-aware routing with automatic model fallback when cost SLO is exceeded

QBR prep checklist (tick items):
- [ ] Table populated for all billable features
- [ ] Confirm 30d metric windows and sampling method
- [ ] Validate cost-per-1k token mapping to pricing tier
- [ ] Add owner and post-QBR action assignee
- [ ] Attach recent logs or rate-limit graphs (screenshot link)

Escalation contacts (example):
- CS lead: Rosa Martinez (rosa@redwood.ai)
- AE: Daniel Park (daniel@redwood.ai)
- Eng on-call: SRE rota via PagerDuty (team: eng-sre)

Notes to reviewer / TODOs for internal use:
- Add a small pivot table on the last sheet to show trend by feature across last 6 months (month, tokens, spend).
- Consider adding a "customer-level behavior" row that describes burst patterns (cron-job/day, user-initiated, onboarding migration).
- Keep this sheet light for QBR slides; move full forensic logs to a linked notebook if needed.

Revision history (internal):
- 2025-02-10: template created by Avery Chen (initial columns and sample rows)
- 2025-02-18: added dedupe recommendation for embedding jobs (Maya Singh)
- 2025-03-04: updated thresholds and alert wording after CS sync (Rosa Martinez)

Example QBR speaking script (30–60s):
"Over the last 30 days we tracked $TOTAL_30D to billable routes. The top three cost drivers are Chat Assist, Report Generation, and Bulk Embeddings, which collectively represent ~78% of spend. Chat Assist had a 48% jump after we paused prefix caching during a canary on Feb 18; we've re-enabled caching and expect cost to normalize within 48 hours. For bulk embeddings, the last migration caused duplicate rows — we recommend a dedupe pass and adding a throttled backfill. We'll follow up with concrete numbers and a proposed schedule in the action tracker."

End of sheet.
